Tab Sync Controller

Tab Sync Controller coordinates cross-tab state negotiation during FeatureCell initialization. When a new browser tab opens, the controller determines whether existing peer tabs hold established state and, if so, synchronizes that state into the new tab before the initial pipeline execution completes.

Tab Sync Contract Summary

  • The controller participates exclusively in the Policy stage during the first pipeline Attempt
  • Peer detection uses a localStorage tab registry to deterministically identify active tabs without relying on timing-sensitive negotiation
  • Each tab maintains a heartbeat that refreshes its registry timestamp at a fixed interval; stale entries are pruned automatically
  • When peers exist, the controller sends a snapshot request via the native browser BroadcastChannel and waits for a peer response or a fixed internal timeout
  • When no peers exist, the controller immediately clears the negotiation cache and abstains, allowing the pipeline to proceed with its initial state
  • After the first Attempt, the controller abstains on all subsequent pipeline messages and responds to snapshot requests from newly opened tabs

The Tab Sync Controller does not observe, derive, or modify state values. Its sole responsibility is to coordinate whether the initial pipeline execution should proceed with bootstrap state or adopt established state from a peer tab. Once negotiation completes, the controller becomes passive and delegates all subsequent cross-tab state broadcasting to the Tab Sync State Behavior.

The Tab Sync system requires both the Tab Sync Controller and the Tab Sync State Behavior to be registered on the same FeatureCell. The controller handles the initial negotiation, while the behavior manages ongoing cross-tab state broadcasting and reception after negotiation completes.

The Tab Sync Controller uses a two-phase broadcast gating mechanism to prevent bootstrap state from overwriting established state in peer tabs. After a ClearCache resolution (no peers responded), the first pipeline finalize enables broadcasting but does not broadcast. Only subsequent pipeline finalizations are broadcast to other tabs. This ensures that a new tab's initial empty or default state is never propagated to existing tabs that hold meaningful data.

License Requirement

Tab Sync requires a valid license . License validation is performed asynchronously at construction time using the license token provided in the behavior context. If validation fails, the behavior is marked as unlicensed and the pipeline rejects it.

Design Decisions

The Tab Sync Controller was designed to solve a specific production failure: browser background-tab throttling makes timing-based negotiation unreliable. When multiple tabs are open, background tabs may be throttled by the browser, causing BroadcastChannel messages to be delayed beyond the negotiation timeout. This led to new tabs incorrectly concluding that no peers existed and broadcasting their bootstrap state, overwriting established state in other tabs.

localStorage Tab Registry

Instead of relying solely on BroadcastChannel responses within a fixed timeout, the controller uses a localStorage tab registry for deterministic peer detection. Each tab registers itself in the registry on construction and maintains a heartbeat that refreshes its timestamp at a fixed interval. When a new tab opens, it reads the registry to determine whether peers exist before deciding whether to send a snapshot request or proceed independently.

This approach eliminates the race condition inherent in timing-based detection: if the registry contains fresh entries, peers definitively exist regardless of whether those tabs respond to BroadcastChannel messages within the timeout window.

Two-Phase Broadcast Gating

When a tab determines it is the first tab online (no peers in the registry), the controller issues a ClearCache command. The behavior sets negotiationComplete to true but leaves broadcastReady as false. The first FinalizePipeline after ClearCache enables broadcastReady but does not broadcast that initial state. Only subsequent pipeline finalizations are broadcast.

This two-phase gating prevents the exact production failure where a new tab's bootstrap state (null or default values) was broadcast to peer tabs, overwriting their established state.

Peer Timeout

When peers are detected in the registry, the controller sends a snapshot request via BroadcastChannel and races a peer response against a fixed internal timeout. If a peer responds with a snapshot, the controller issues a CommitCache command and aborts the initial pipeline Attempt. If the timeout expires before any peer responds, the controller falls back to ClearCache and abstains.

Settling Period

After receiving a peer snapshot and issuing CommitCache, the controller enters a brief settling period during which subsequent Attempt messages are aborted. This prevents the tab's bootstrap pipelines from executing and potentially broadcasting stale initial state before the synced state has been fully committed.

Degraded Mode

If the BroadcastChannel API or localStorage is unavailable, the Tab Sync Controller degrades gracefully — it immediately clears the negotiation cache and abstains, allowing the pipeline to proceed with bootstrap state. The behavior continues to operate as standard Core State. No errors are thrown and no pipeline execution is blocked. The FeatureCell functions normally as a single-tab state container.

This makes Tab Sync safe to use in server-side rendering (SSR), Node.js services, Deno, web workers, and any other runtime where browser-specific APIs are not present. The same FeatureCell configuration works across all environments without conditional logic or feature detection.

Diagrams
Configuration

The Tab Sync Controller operates within the Policy stage during the first pipeline Attempt. It uses a localStorage tab registry for deterministic peer detection and BroadcastChannel for cross-tab snapshot exchange.

The controller does not require explicit configuration options. Peer detection, heartbeat intervals, stale thresholds, and timeout durations are managed internally with production-tested defaults.

Tab Sync requires both a controller and a behavior to be registered on the same FeatureCell. The controller handles the initial cross-tab negotiation, while the behavior manages ongoing state broadcasting and reception after negotiation completes.

Tab Sync Controller
Controller Description Package
withTabSyncController

type: controller

 Coordinates initial cross-tab state negotiation using a localStorage tab registry for peer detection and BroadcastChannel for snapshot exchange. On the first pipeline Attempt, the controller determines whether to adopt peer state or proceed independently. After negotiation, the controller abstains on all subsequent Attempts and responds to snapshot requests from newly opened tabs.
Internal Configuration Constants
Constant Description
TAB_SYNC_PEER_TIMEOUT Maximum time (in milliseconds) to wait for a peer snapshot response before falling back to ClearCache. Default: 3,000ms.
TAB_SYNC_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL Interval (in milliseconds) at which each tab refreshes its registry timestamp. Default: 5,000ms.
TAB_SYNC_STALE_THRESHOLD Maximum age (in milliseconds) of a registry entry before it is considered stale and pruned. Default: 15,000ms.
TAB_SYNC_REGISTRY_PREFIX localStorage key prefix for the tab registry. Combined with the featureCellKey to produce a unique registry key per FeatureCell.
Registering the Tab Sync Controller

The Tab Sync Controller and Tab Sync State Behavior are attached structurally when the FeatureCell is defined. Both must be present for cross-tab synchronization to function.

Unlike other controllers such as Throttle or Delay, the Tab Sync Controller does not require fluent API configuration during initialization. Registration alone is sufficient to enable cross-tab state negotiation. 

{{`export const appConfig: ApplicationConfig = {
  providers: [
    provideVault({ logLevel: 'off' }),

    provideFeatureCell(
      EmployeeService,
      {
        key: 'employees',
        initialState: [],
      },
      [
        // Tab Sync State Behavior is required
        withTabSyncStateBehavior
      ],
      [
        // Tab Sync Controller is required
        withTabSyncController
      ]
    )
  ]
};`}}
 
{{`export const employeeCell = FeatureCell<Employee[]>(
  {
    key: 'employees',
    initialState: [],
  },
  [
    // Tab Sync State Behavior is required
    withTabSyncStateBehavior
  ],
  [
    // Tab Sync Controller is required
    withTabSyncController
  ]
);`}}

FeatureCell Initialization

The Tab Sync Controller activates automatically when the FeatureCell is initialized. No additional fluent API calls are required. The controller registers itself in the localStorage tab registry, starts its heartbeat, opens the BroadcastChannel, and subscribes to bus notifications during construction.

When .initialize() is called on the FeatureCell, the first pipeline Attempt triggers the negotiation flow. The controller reads the tab registry, determines whether peers exist, and coordinates state synchronization before the initial pipeline completes. 

{{`
@FeatureCell<Employee[]>('employees')
@Injectable({
  providedIn: 'root'
})
export class EmployeeService {
  private readonly vault = injectVault<Employee[]>(EmployeeService);

  constructor() {
    // Tab Sync activates automatically on initialize
    this.vault.initialize();
  }
}`}}
 
{{`
// Tab Sync activates automatically on initialize
employeeCell.initialize();`}}
 
{{`
// Tab Sync activates automatically on initialize
employeeCell.initialize();`}}
When to Use Tab Sync Controller

Tab Sync is designed for applications where users commonly work with multiple browser tabs open simultaneously and state consistency across tabs is a requirement. Common use cases include:

  • Multi-tab dashboards — ensuring all tabs reflect the same data after a user performs an action in any single tab
  • Form state continuity — preventing data loss when a user opens a new tab and expects to see the same form state
  • Session-wide settings — synchronizing user preferences, theme selections, or configuration changes across all open tabs
  • Collaborative workflows — keeping shared application state consistent when multiple tabs interact with the same backend resources

Tab Sync is not a replacement for server-side state synchronization. It operates exclusively within the browser using localStorage and BroadcastChannel. State changes are synchronized between tabs on the same origin in the same browser. Cross-browser, cross-device, or cross-origin synchronization requires a server-side solution.

Negotiation Flow

The Tab Sync Controller executes its negotiation logic exclusively on the first pipeline Attempt. The flow differs based on whether peers are detected in the localStorage tab registry.

No Peers Detected

When the registry contains no fresh entries from other tabs, the controller immediately issues a ClearCache command and votes Abstain. No BroadcastChannel messages are sent. The behavior enables negotiationComplete and begins the two-phase broadcast gating sequence.

Peers Detected

When the registry contains fresh entries from other tabs, the controller sends a snapshot request via BroadcastChannel and races two outcomes:

  • Peer responds — the controller issues a CommitCache command with the received snapshot, enters the settling period, and votes Abort. The behavior applies the peer snapshot directly and enables broadcastReady immediately.
  • Timeout expires — the controller issues a ClearCache command and votes Abstain. The behavior proceeds with the two-phase broadcast gating sequence.
Negotiation Outcomes
Registry State Peer Response Bus Command Vote broadcastReady
No peers N/A ClearCache Abstain Deferred (enabled after first FinalizePipeline)
Peers exist Snapshot received CommitCache Abort Immediate
Peers exist Timeout ClearCache Abstain Deferred (enabled after first FinalizePipeline)
Graceful Degradation

The Tab Sync Controller degrades gracefully when browser APIs are unavailable:

  • BroadcastChannel unavailable — the controller immediately issues ClearCache and abstains. The FeatureCell operates as if Tab Sync is not configured.
  • localStorage unavailable — the controller skips registry operations and falls back to the no-peers fast path. Heartbeat and beforeunload cleanup are silently skipped.

In all degradation scenarios, the FeatureCell continues to function normally as a single-tab state container. No errors are thrown and no pipeline execution is blocked.

Examples

Tab Sync is enabled by registering both the Tab Sync Controller and the Tab Sync State Behavior during FeatureCell definition. No additional fluent API configuration is required.

Example 1: Complete Tab Sync Configuration

In this example, a FeatureCell is configured with Tab Sync. When the application opens in a new tab, the controller checks for existing peer tabs. If a peer responds with a snapshot, the new tab adopts the peer's state. If no peers exist, the tab proceeds with its initial state. After negotiation, all tabs broadcast state changes to each other automatically. 

{{`// app.config.ts

export const appConfig: ApplicationConfig = {
  providers: [
    provideVault({ logLevel: 'off' }),

    provideFeatureCell(
      EmployeeService,
      {
        key: 'employees',
        initialState: [],
      },
      [
        // Tab Sync State Behavior handles broadcasting and receiving
        withTabSyncStateBehavior
      ],
      [
        // Tab Sync Controller handles initial negotiation
        withTabSyncController
      ]
    )
  ]
};

@FeatureCell<Employee[]>('employees')
@Injectable({
  providedIn: 'root'
})
export class EmployeeService {
  private readonly vault = injectVault<Employee[]>(EmployeeService);

  constructor() {
    // Tab Sync activates automatically — no fluent API required
    this.vault.initialize();
  }
}`}}
 
{{`export const employeeCell = FeatureCell<Employee[]>(
  {
    key: 'employees',
    initialState: [],
  },
  [
    // Tab Sync State Behavior handles broadcasting and receiving
    withTabSyncStateBehavior
  ],
  [
    // Tab Sync Controller handles initial negotiation
    withTabSyncController
  ]
);

// Tab Sync activates automatically — no fluent API required
employeeCell.initialize();`}}
 
{{`export const employeeCell = FeatureCell<Employee[]>(
